entry_point: MCP tools (docs, memory, templates) and the web UI HTTP template-preview route; Go API: the storage-layer stores that turn a caller name into a file under the project knowledge base

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit: a document folder/path, memory identifier, template name, or template-preview file argument containing parent-segment spelling causes the storage layer to create, read, write, move or delete a file outside that record kind's own subdirectory. Driven through the real MCP tool handlers and the web UI HTTP routes exactly as the project's own tests do (storage.NewStore, store.Init, handle* via mcp.CallToolRequest, httptest for the preview route). No server process, no network, no services.
sites: internal/storage/doc_store.go — document path joined onto the documents directory (create folder, get, update, delete); the published-fix site the report leads to
internal/storage/memory_store.go — memory identifier joined onto the memory directory as a prefixed markdown filename (get, delete, promote/move); published-fix far site
internal/storage/template_store.go — template name joined onto the templates directory (create, get, including import-qualified names); published-fix far site
internal/server/routes/templates.go — template-preview file argument joined onto that template's directory; published-fix far site
routes: No pattern-B uncovered route (unmodified upstream code reaching the sink with the protection missing) was found: at the pinned commit every name-to-file mapping lacks the confinement uniformly, so there is no 'already-covered-elsewhere' route to lean on. The additional levers are injected siblings (track=injected), registered below.
injected_siblings: internal/storage/doc_archive.go — new document-archive operation that copies a document into the project's archive area keyed by the document's path; reached through a new action on the documentation tool
internal/storage/memory_history.go — new memory-revision-history side record keyed by the memory identifier, in the versions area; reached through new actions on the memory tool
verified.project_tests_run: internal/models, internal/storage, internal/mcp/handlers, internal/server/routes — the project's own suites pass unchanged on both the injected and the oracle tree (signature-stable fix). Hidden security tests: 13/13 fail on the injected tree, 13/13 pass on the oracle tree. Hidden functional tests: 8/8 pass on both. CGO_ENABLED=1 is required (an optional embedding dependency); recorded in the Dockerfile and test.sh.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a panic aborts the Go test binary so the suite cannot pass, and the web preview tests require a client error while rejecting 5xx, so a crash-turned-500 cannot satisfy the refusal contract.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: each operation confines the exact record path it is about to touch; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource that could be authorised instead of the file the operation reads or writes.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every site is one name-to-file mapping shared by create, read, update and delete; a verb-only guard is a partial application of that mapping, and the per-site miss-patches already leave that site's create/get/delete tests failing together.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the containment is the first thing applied to the caller name; there is no earlier lossy normalisation step a fix could place its check after and silently defeat.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is purely lexical; there is no external authority that could return nothing and make the guard fail open.

traps.lever: base flaw / published-fix site (pattern A, report target)
traps.shape: caller-supplied document folder and path joined onto the documents directory; shapes: create with a parent-segment folder, get and delete with a parent-segment path, and a symlink inside the documents directory pointing outside
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none — this is the site the report leads to; the lever is that a purely lexical parent-segment fix still misses the symlink shape and the create/delete verbs

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, second record kind)
traps.shape: caller-supplied memory identifier becomes a prefixed markdown filename under the memory directory; parent-segment spelling escapes once the prefix absorbs a segment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about documents; memory is another tool and another directory, and a one-segment parent reference looks harmless because the filename prefix absorbs it

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, stored-identity producer)
traps.shape: an identifier already recorded in a stored record's own on-disk metadata is reused when that record is moved between layers; the filename builder does not call the parser that produced the identifier
traps.reason_to_dismiss: "the identifier came from our own file, and was accepted when the record was read"

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, neighbouring feature + web UI)
traps.shape: template name joined onto the templates directory (create/get, including import-qualified names) and the web interface's template-preview file argument joined onto that template's directory
traps.reason_to_dismiss: templates are a neighbouring feature the report does not name; the preview is the web interface, not the assistant tools

traps.shape: new document-archive operation copies a document into the project's archive area keyed by the document's path; parent-segment spelling carries that copy outside
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a derived copy in a separate archive area, not the live documents the report is about; a solver who confines the live document path assumes the copy is routed through it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code idiom: the project already keeps side records outside the live document directory, and a path-keyed archive copy matches the surrounding storage style with no tell-tale names

traps.shape: new memory-revision-history side record keyed by the memory identifier, in the versions area; parent-segment spelling on the identifier writes or reads outside that area
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a read of a system side-record in a different area; guarding the live record's own read/write is what the report asks for
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code idiom: the project already keeps a versions-style side record for another entity kind, and a small history file keyed by the same identifier is the obvious parity feature
